Figure 1:MolRSI motivation and architecture.(a) Molecular discovery involves a combinatorial space of decisions across preparation, generation and prioritization, illustrated forde novoprotein binder design. Nodes represent options at each stage. The orange path traces one possible workflow.
(b) Scientists accumulate lessons from experimental outcomes across projects, learning to avoid unproductive choices and focus exploration on promising regions.
(c)MolRSIcouples systematic workflow search with persistent cross-task memory. The Explore agent retrieves relevant resources from scientific literature and code repositories, then converts them into reusable, executable skills through implementation and validation. Workflow evaluations update solution memory (workflows and performance), refinement memory (modifications and their effects) and execution memory (execution strategies and repairs). Accumulated experience guides subsequent workflow selection, refinement and execution, recursively improving the effective search policy fromπt\pi_{t}toπt+1\pi_{t+1}. Colored paths indicate evaluated workflows, faded elements denote deprioritized choices, and orange-outlined nodes represent new local options. Projects, outcomes and memory entries are illustrative.

Figure 2:Computational evaluation ofMolRSIfor antibiotic discovery.(a) Test AUPRC and rankings ofMolRSIwithout RSI and baseline agents across six antibacterial tasks.
(b) Resource library.
(c) Experience from 25 source tasks, excluding the antibacterial targets.
(d) Search trajectories over 20 iterations.
(e) Search with and without RSI and zero-search transfer, which retains model fitting and validation.
(f) Zero-search transfer performance versus memory-pool size. The line shows test AUPRC averaged analytically across the six held-out antibacterial tasks and all possible subsets of each size from the 25-task memory pool. Darker and lighter shading indicate the interquartile range (IQR; 25th–75th percentiles) and the 5th–95th percentile range, respectively, across 2,000 sampled memory subsets at each pool size. In (a,d,e), means and±1\pm 1sample SD are shown across five data splits. Circles in (a) denote individual splits.

Figure 3:Virtual screening and experimental validation with MolRSI.(a) Screening workflow yielding 107 tested compounds; cytotoxicity-filter exceptions are detailed inSectionS3.4.
(b) t-SNE projection [?] of training and tested compounds; stars indicate hits.
(c) Activity-score ranking of tested compounds.
(d) MSSA and MRSA MICs and HepG2, HSkMC and IMR-90CC50\mathrm{CC}_{50}values for two selected hits, C3 and C32; dots show individual MIC measurements.
(e) Hit rates for 107MolRSI-selected and 241 expert-selected compounds [?], with 95% Wilson confidence intervals.
(f) AUROC and AUPRC on the shared 271-compound held-outS. aureustest set.
(g) Chemical structures and dose–response curves of C3 and C32. Symbols show responses; lines indicate descriptive logistic fits. Two response series are shown per curve. Hits are defined by an MSSA MIC of 32μ\mug/mL or lower.

Figure 4:Benchmarking and experience-guided optimization of pMHC binder-design workflows.(a) Enrichment Factor (EF) at the top-ranked 1% and 2% cutoffs (EF@1% and EF@2%) forMolRSIand four agent baselines across 14 miniprotein-binder tasks. Heatmaps show individual tasks; bars show the unweighted macro average across tasks.
(b) Protein resource library organized into input preparation, generation, sequence design and assessment, structure prediction, scoring and score combination.
(c) EF@1% and EF@2% on the held-out MART-1 pMHC target forMolRSIwith and without RSI and four agent baselines.
(d) Best-so-far search objective, defined as the mean ranking score among the top 5% of candidates, during MART-1 and SARS-CoV-1 design-workflow optimization.
(e) On-target versus off-target scores for selected MART-1 and SARS-CoV-1 designs fromMolRSIand Claude Science, evaluated with theMolRSIranking score (left) and Claude Science score (right).

Figure 5:Prospective experimental validation of pMHC binder designs.Upper and lower rows in a–c show MART-1 and SARS-CoV-1, respectively.
(a) On-target log2FC and its difference from the maximum available off-target log2FC. Dashed lines mark hit thresholds (x>4x>4,y>0y>0); legend values indicate hits/evaluable designs. (b) UMAP [?] of predicted minibinder structures based on TM-align [?] similarity; stars mark experimental hits. (c) Designs ranked byMolRSIscore, with hits highlighted in green. (d) Predicted complexes of sars1_0101 and mart1_0014. Minibinders, MHC and peptides are blue, orange and pink, respectively; yellow dashed lines indicate candidate polar contacts.
